Description

Action potentials arriving at nociceptor terminals release glutamate, substance P, CGRP and BDNF, centrally in the dorsal horn and peripherally in the joint. In the joint the released neuropeptides act back on mast cells, which degranulate and release mediators that sensitise the same nerve endings, a loop known as neurogenic inflammation. Substance P reaches human mast cells mainly through MRGPRX2, and mast cells are abundant and activated in osteoarthritic synovium.

Colour

Proteins and metabolites are coloured by their contribution to pain: red for those that raise it (they excite or sensitise nociceptive neurons, or drive the inflammation that does), blue for those that relieve it, and olive for the shared signalling machinery (G proteins, RGS, adenylate cyclase, phospholipases, kinases, adaptors, second messengers, ions and nucleotides), whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block, so the same molecule can be red in one block and blue in another.

The transmitters, their receptors and the receptor of substance P on mast cells (MRGPRX2) are red: released from nociceptors they activate mast cells and carry nociceptive signals. CGRP, red here, is anti-inflammatory on macrophages, where it inhibits the production of TNF (Feng 1997).
